bio-text:
I am an archivist at the Federal University of Bahia (UFBA), currently seconded to the National Archives as Head of the Northeast Regional Office (2025–). I coordinate the Farinha and Arquivos da UFBA projects. I am interested in the interfaces between Archival Science, Digital Humanities, Hacker Culture, and Artificial Intelligence applied to archives.

Since 2024, I have been working at LABHDUFBA (Digital Humanities Laboratory at UFBA). I was coordinator of CRIDI (Study Group on Culture, Representation, and Digital Information) between 2019 and 2026, a group I have been a member of since 2008, currently inactive. My trajectory combines archival practice — working in records management, digital preservation, and archival description — with applied research in AI, network analysis, and data visualization applied to documentary collections.

about-bio-p1: Master's in Information Science and Bachelor's in Archival Science from the Federal University of Bahia (UFBA). Currently serves as Head of the Northeast Regional Office (ERE-NE) of the National Archives (2025–) and is a civil servant at UFBA, where he works as an archivist, currently seconded to the National Archives. He coordinates the Farinha project, a free software platform for creating access systems for permanent and memorial collections, and Arquivos da UFBA, an integration and access platform for the archives and collections of the Federal University of Bahia.
about-bio-p2: His career focuses on collection management, technical processing of archival information, and the development of initiatives for access, dissemination, and innovation. He has experience in archival description, information representation, and the development of digital platforms for access to collections, including initiatives using artificial intelligence (agents and RAG).
about-bio-p3: Since 2024, he has been working at LABHDUFBA (Digital Humanities Laboratory at UFBA). He was coordinator of CRIDI (Study Group on Culture, Representation, and Digital Information) between 2019 and 2026, a group he has been a member of since 2008. He has also been part of the research groups GEPICC (2003–2008) and GEPINDI (2004–2007).
about-bio-p4: His work spans the interfaces between Archival Science, Digital Humanities, information access, hacker culture, and technologies applied to archives, with applied research in AI, network analysis, and data visualization applied to documentary collections. He is a ham radio operator (PU6RIC), holds Brazilian and Portuguese nationality, and was an elected delegate for the 1st CNARQ and a designated delegate for the 2nd CNARQ (National Conference on Archives).
